Held-out evidence: 641 FPs; median contrast 20.4 vs 0.2 in TN, and P95 77.2 vs 3.0.
Physical explanation: Bronchus, tissue edge or heterogeneous contact can create a local peak.
Clinical use: CT-prior plus repeat palpation; use size/depth plausibility.

Held-out evidence: 103 FNs; median contrast 5.3 vs 24.5 in TP, with drift 0.044 vs 0.017.
Physical explanation: Tangential touch, attenuation and local slip suppress center-border contrast.
Clinical use: Resweep CT-marked region; do not exclude on one low-P frame.

Held-out evidence: Overall size Top-2 = 90.6%; the hardest exact bin is 1.25 cm (36.4% exact, 67.3% Top-2).
Physical explanation: Larger, around-1-cm nodules deform under pressure, so amplitude and footprint do not scale perfectly.
Clinical use: Report an adjacent interval or Top-2 range instead of a single exact size class.

Held-out evidence: Deep exact = 51.9%, deep Top-2 = 66.1%; overall depth Top-2 = 85.2%.
Physical explanation: Deep responses are attenuated and can shift when the nodule slides inside the phantom/tissue.
Clinical use: Use depth as auxiliary guidance, not as a hard exclusion boundary.
